issues.failure_explanation: As written, (eqn:in1) is false: for constants sigma_1<sigma_2, Property 2 gives <(Lambda_{sigma_1}-Lambda_{sigma_2})g,g> >= 0, while the claimed upper bound int(sigma_1-sigma_2)|grad u_2|^2 is negative for g != 0. The correct inequality has the middle term <(Lambda_{sigma_2}-Lambda_{sigma_1})g,g> (equivalently, int(sigma_2-sigma_1)|grad u_2|^2 <= <(Lambda_1-Lambda_2)g,g> <= int (sigma_2/sigma_1)(sigma_2-sigma_1)|grad u_2|^2). With sigma_1=sigma_D, sigma_2=sigma_bg, the stated (eqn:in1) only gives the negative lower bound int_D (sigma_bg/sigma_a)(sigma_a-sigma_bg)|grad u_bg|^2, so (eqn:lem1) does not follow from the premise as stated. It follows from the correct version, which Section 6 quotes.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace (eqn:in1) by the correct standard inequality, with <(Lambda_{sigma_2}-Lambda_{sigma_1})g,g> in the middle. Then (eqn:lem1) follows verbatim.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the main lemma rests on a false displayed inequality. The lemma's conclusion and the Section 6 bounds remain valid once the standard inequality is used.
issues.title: Key energy inequality (eqn:in1) stated with the wrong sign; (eqn:lem1) does not follow from it
issues.why_classification: This is a local correction of a cited standard inequality. The lemma, its proof structure and the constant k_1 are all unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\Omega$ be a connected open subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$, with $n = 2,3$, and $A\subset\Omega$

issues.failure_explanation: The only hypothesis on A is that A is a subset of Omega. Taking A a single point (or the empty set), every solution u is constant on A, yet non-constant solutions exist. Weak unique continuation requires A to be a nonempty open set, or at least of positive measure.

failure_location.quote: If $u$ is constant in $A$, then $u$ is constant in $\Omega$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that A is a nonempty open subset of Omega, and apply the theorem to a connected component of the open set D.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem is false as stated. Its use in the nonexistence argument requires D to have nonempty interior, which the statement does not encode.
issues.title: Weak UCP stated for an arbitrary subset A
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard missing hypothesis restores the cited result. Nothing else in the paper changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Throughout this paper, $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, with $n\geq2$, is the region occupied by the conducting material.
with $\sigma\in L^{\infty}_+(\Omega)$ for $n=2$ or $\sigma$ Lipschitz continuous for $n=3$
Unfortunately, such boundary data $g$ does not exists.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper's setting allows any n>=2 and any sigma_bg in L^infty_+. The invoked theorem covers only n=2, or n=3 with Lipschitz sigma. For n=3 with merely bounded sigma_bg, and for n>=4, the claimed nonexistence of nonzero g in the kernel of Lambda_{sigma_D}-Lambda_{sigma_bg} is not supported by the cited result.

failure_location.quote: As a direct consequence of the UCP stated in Theorem~\ref{teo:ucp}, it is not possible to find a non-constant boundary data $g$ fulfilling~\eqref{eqn:idcond}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the nonexistence claim to n=2, or to Lipschitz sigma_bg in higher dimensions with an appropriate UCP reference, or state it conditionally on UCP holding for sigma_bg.
issues.overall_effect: The stated impossibility motivating the approximate (eigenfunction) approach is unsupported in part of the advertised setting.
issues.title: Nonexistence of kernel data asserted beyond the scope of the stated UCP
issues.why_classification: The claim only needs a stated scope restriction. The method and the numerics (2D) are unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The same result can be proved for $\sigma_a^m>\sigma_{bg}^M$, with similar arguments.
it is possible to select an eigenfunction $g_n$ corresponding to an arbitrary small eigenvalue $\lambda_n$

issues.failure_explanation: When sigma_a^m > sigma_bg^M, sigma_D >= sigma_bg, so by Property 2 Lambda_{sigma_D}-Lambda_{sigma_bg} <= 0. Its eigenvalues are then nonpositive and increase to zero, so they are not 'monotonically decreasing to zero'. Selecting an 'arbitrarily small' eigenvalue would pick the most negative one, i.e. the worst boundary data. A threshold eps proportional to lambda_n<0 yields an empty reconstruction, and the analytic radius formula takes a root of a negative number.

failure_location.quote: such that $\{\lambda_n\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is monotonically decreasing to zero

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Order the eigenvalues by modulus and use |lambda_n| (equivalently, apply the method to the operator Lambda_{sigma_bg}-Lambda_{sigma_D}) in the selection rule and thresholds when sigma_a > sigma_bg.
issues.overall_effect: As stated, the reconstruction procedure only works for sigma_a < sigma_bg, although the setting and the lemma advertise both well-separated cases.
issues.title: Spectral ordering and eigenvalue-based selection/threshold fail in the advertised regime sigma_a > sigma_bg
issues.why_classification: A sign/absolute-value adjustment restores the procedure in both regimes with the same method and guarantees.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Indeed, if $u_{bg}$ is constant in $D$, then it results to be constant over $\Omega$
The method relies on the possibility to find a boundary data $g$ producing a vanishing electric field in the regions occupied by the anomaly
We provide a simple manner to evaluate this special boundary data $g$
Beside theoretical results and justifications of our method

issues.failure_explanation: By the paper's own UCP argument, the kernel is {0}. The orthonormal g_n stay at distance 1 from it, so they approximate no kernel element; the conclusions' claim to 'evaluate this special boundary data g' contradicts the proven nonexistence. What is established is only int_D sigma_bg|grad u_bg|^2 <= lambda_n/k_1. Since g_n tends weakly to 0 and Lambda_bg is compact, the total power <Lambda_bg g_n,g_n> over all of Omega also tends to 0. The bound therefore does not show that the power density is small in D relative to Omega\D, and no result links the sublevel set tilde D to D.

failure_location.quote: In other words, the eigenfunctions $g_n$ related to \emph{small} eigenvalues represent a good approximation of an element of $\ker\{\Lambda_{\sigma_D}-\Lambda_{\sigma_{bg}}\}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reformulate the claims: the g_n are almost-null vectors (small Rayleigh quotient), and the region rule is a heuristic supported by the integral bound and the examples. Drop the claims that the method finds g with vanishing field in D or approximates kernel elements.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised theoretical justification of the reconstruction (low-power region approximates D) is heuristic. Only the analytic concentric examples support it.
issues.title: Claimed approximation of kernel elements and theoretical justification are not established
issues.why_classification: No reconstruction guarantee survives. The claimed theoretical justification must be withdrawn, a limited but material weakening of the advertised content, though the method and numerics remain.

issues.failure_explanation: The Weyl/min-max bound requires N self-adjoint. For a general bounded N, Lambda_n can have non-real eigenvalues: on a repeated eigenvalue mu, the perturbation delta*[[0,1],[-1,0]] produces mu±i*delta. Then 'ordered in a decreasing order' is meaningless, and an ordered matching with constant 1 is not available in general. If N is not compact, Lambda_n may have essential spectrum and no decreasing eigenvalue sequence.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume N is self-adjoint, as the symmetric noise matrix in the numerics is, and state the bound for the min-max values (or assume N compact). It then follows from Weyl's inequality.
issues.overall_effect: The noise analysis underlying the plateau-based eigenvalue selection rests on a proposition that is false or ill-posed under the stated noise model.
issues.title: Eigenvalue perturbation bound claimed for a merely bounded (non-self-adjoint) noise operator
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard hypothesis, already satisfied by the numerical noise model, restores the stated bound unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The upper inequality only gives P-P_b <= sup((sigma_bg-sigma_a)/sigma_a) * int_D sigma_bg|grad u|^2 <= ((sigma_bg^M-sigma_a^m)/sigma_a^m) * int_D sigma_bg|grad u|^2. Hence the lower bound has constant sigma_a^m/(sigma_bg^M-sigma_a^m). The claimed constant sigma_a^m/(sigma_bg^m-sigma_a^M) is larger whenever the conductivities are non-constant. The required pointwise bound (sigma_bg-sigma_a)/sigma_a <= Delta_sigma/sigma_a^m fails, e.g. where sigma_a = sigma_a^m.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace sigma_a^m/Delta_sigma by sigma_a^m/(sigma_bg^M-sigma_a^m) in (eqn:sogp3) and in the alpha-interval. The alpha=1 condition then becomes sigma_bg^M > 2 sigma_a^m, which is unchanged for uniform materials.
issues.overall_effect: The admissible alpha-interval for the threshold, and the condition sigma_bg^m > sigma_a^m+sigma_a^M in the subsequent Remark, are unsupported for inhomogeneous sigma_a or sigma_bg.
issues.title: Lower bound in (eqn:sogp3) uses an unjustified constant
issues.why_classification: This is a local constant correction. The structure of the threshold rule and the practical conclusion survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: So the threshold has to be chosen as
The educated guess of Section~\ref{sec:anex}, $\varepsilon=\lambda_n\lVert g_n \rVert_2^2$, i.e. $\alpha=1$

issues.failure_explanation: (eqn:sogp3) bounds the integral of the power density over D, which is a power. Yet (eqn:thr) prescribes the pointwise density threshold eps itself as alpha*lambda_n*||g_n||^2, which is dimensionally and logically a different object. Section 5 did not set eps=lambda_k; it imposed the integral condition, and there the density level at tilde r_i is p = k lambda_k/(pi tilde r_i^2) (R=1), not lambda_k. The final algorithm (eqn:thr2) again uses the integral condition.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the rule as: choose eps so that the sublevel set tilde D={p<eps} satisfies int_{tilde D} p = alpha*lambda_n*||g_n||^2 with alpha in the admissible interval, consistent with (eqn:thr2), and correct the Remark accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The analytically derived threshold rule is a non sequitur and is inconsistent with both Section 5 and the final algorithm.
issues.title: Bound on integrated power in D turned into a pointwise power-density threshold
issues.why_classification: This is a local reformulation matching what the final algorithm already does. No loss of method or claims.
